entry.title: The mod-two square algebra, admissible sequences, and excess
entry.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Let $T=\mathbb F_2\langle s_1,s_2,\ldots\rangle$ be the vector space with basis the finite words in the symbols $s_j$ for $j>0$, including the empty word, and with multiplication the bilinear extension of concatenation. Concatenation is associative and the empty word is its unit, so this explicitly constructs the free associative graded algebra, with $|s_j|=j$ and $s_0=1$. Define $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ as its quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by

$$s_a s_b+\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor a/2\rfloor} \binom{b-j-1}{a-2j}s_{a+b-j}s_j, \qquad 0<a<2b.$$

A normalized sequence $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ has positive entries; the empty sequence denotes the unit. It is admissible if $i_j\ge 2i_{j+1}$. Write $|I|=\sum_j i_j$, put $i_{k+1}=0$, and define

$$d_j(I)=i_j-2i_{j+1},\qquad e(I)=\sum_{j=1}^k d_j(I)=i_1-i_2-\cdots-i_k.$$

For the empty sequence set $|I|=e(I)=0$. The square algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is the image of the free algebra under $s_j\mapsto Sq^j$ in natural mod-two cohomology operations, allowing every nonnegative input degree. The published Adem theorem makes the induced map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ well defined. The admissible-composites theorem proves it is an isomorphism.

Every relation is homogeneous. A quotient by a two-sided ideal is a unital associative graded algebra: products of cosets are independent of representatives since multiplying an ideal element on either side remains in the ideal. Its grading is the direct sum of homogeneous quotient spaces since the generating relations are homogeneous. The displayed finite sums defining degree and excess are unambiguous; admissibility makes each $d_j$ nonnegative. Composition and addition of the published natural linear operations preserve naturality, so the image algebra exists. Each square commutes with suspension by the published normalization/suspension proposition, so the resulting composites are stable wherever their source degrees are defined. No assertion that *every* stable operation is such a composite is needed for this definition.
entry.strategy: Construct the free associative word algebra by concatenation, then take its quotient by the homogeneous two-sided Adem ideal. Verify representative independence, associativity, the unit and quotient grading directly. Define degree, admissibility and excess by finite sums, including the empty word; the nonnegative admissibility differences telescope to excess. The published Adem relations give the quotient-to-square-operation map. Naturality, linearity, composition and the published suspension identity give its stable image algebra. Spanning, independence and the presentation are proved by Items 2–4; no classification of all stable operations is assumed.

entry.title: Local path-fibration and cohomology inputs for mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane induction
entry.statement: Assume AC. For $q\ge2$, $K_q$ is simply connected, $\widetilde H^j(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $j<q$, and $H^q(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2\iota_q$. The actual contractible mapping-path fibration has strict loop fiber $F=\Omega K_q$. There is a marked weak equivalence $h:K_{q-1}\to F$ inducing an isomorphism of mod-two cohomology rings $h^*:H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(K_{q-1};\mathbb F_2)$. Its natural multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequence has constant fiber system. No claim that $F$ has CW homotopy type or that $h$ is a homotopy equivalence is needed. In particular its abutment vanishes in positive degrees.
entry.strategy: Use ordinary Hurewicz and cohomology UCT on the CW base to obtain its lower vanishing and normalized first class. Apply direct mapping-path factorization to the marked basepoint inclusion; the actual total contracts, and the fibration LES computes the connected strict loop fiber's marking and homotopy groups. Extend its basepoint by a weak CW approximation, identify that CW model with the marked K(F_2,q-1) by uniqueness, and adjust the uniqueness map to be based via the CW-point cofibration and moving-basepoint formula. Their composite is a marked weak equivalence. The published weak-equivalence homology lemma, natural coefficient UCT and field duality make its cohomology map an isomorphism; cup naturality makes it a ring isomorphism. Apply the multiplicative Serre theorem to the actual fibration with trivial monodromy. No strict-fiber CW-type theorem is imported.

entry.title: Infinite real projective space is a marked mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane space
entry.statement: Assume AC. Infinite real projective space, with the marking of its fundamental group given by the nontrivial antipodal deck transformation, is a CW $K(\mathbb F_2,1)$. Its degree-one ring generator is its normalized mod-two fundamental class, so its cohomology is $\mathbb F_2[\iota_1]$.
entry.strategy: Identify the stable sphere and rank-one Grassmannian models. Coordinate-positive unit representatives give local sections of the antipodal double cover; their finite-stage formulas are continuous in the weak topologies. The covering homotopy-lifting theorem makes it a fibration, and stable Stiefel contractibility gives no higher base homotopy. Endpoint deck transformations identify the fundamental group with Z/2, with injectivity from a contraction of a closed lifted loop and surjectivity from a path joining antipodes. Schubert cells give the CW structure. The published polynomial projective-space cohomology ring has a unique nonzero degree-one class, which is therefore the normalized fundamental class. Marked uniqueness transfers it to the chosen CW model.

entry.title: Steenrod squares commute with relative cohomology connectors
entry.statement: For every pair $(E,F)$, the mod-two cohomology connector satisfies $\delta Sq^a(x)=Sq^a\delta(x)$ for every $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and every nonnegative $a$. Relative squares use the published relative cup-$i$ construction.
entry.strategy: Extend a fiber cocycle u by zero to a cochain b on the ambient space and put c=db, a relative representative of the connector. For 0≤a≤m set j=m-a. The cochain b cup_(j+1) db + b cup_j b restricts to a representative of Sq^a[u], and the published cup-i coboundary identity makes its coboundary c cup_(j+1) c, representing Sq^a[c]. At a=m+1 use the relative primitive b cup_0 db; larger operations vanish by instability. The relative carrier property and characteristic two justify all cancellations and relative representatives, including degree-zero inputs.

entry.title: Fiber and limit isomorphisms force a base-axis isomorphism
entry.statement:
Let $\Phi:\bar E\to E$ be a morphism of first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequences of vector spaces, with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and

$$\bar E_2^{p,q}=\bar E_2^{p,0}\otimes\bar E_2^{0,q},\qquad E_2^{p,q}=E_2^{p,0}\otimes E_2^{0,q}.$$

Assume $\Phi_2$ factors as the tensor product of its axis maps, the fiber-axis map is an isomorphism, and $\Phi_\infty$ is an isomorphism in every position. Then the base-axis map $\Phi_2^{p,0}$ is an isomorphism in every degree.
entry.strategy: Induct on the base column k. The tensor factorization and fiber-axis isomorphism give E_2 isomorphisms through that column. Induction on r yields page-r isomorphisms in columns p≤k-r+1 and injections in columns p≤k, by comparing cycles and incoming boundaries. At the next bottom position (k+1,0), compare the incoming-differential exact sequences. For each incoming source, use finite downward induction from its stationary limit to prove surjectivity on its cycle subgroup; later outgoing differentials have negative fiber target. Starting from the limiting bottom isomorphism, descend in r using this cycle surjectivity and the other exact-sequence isomorphisms. This proves the next E_2 base-column isomorphism and closes the induction.

entry.title: A connected graded module coalgebra with injective unit orbit is free
entry.statement: Assume AC and fix a field $k$. Let $A=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}A_i$ be a unital associative graded $k$-algebra with $A_0=k1_A$, equipped with a degree-preserving coassociative counital coproduct $\Delta_A$ such that $\Delta_A(1_A)=1_A\otimes1_A$ and $\Delta_A,\varepsilon_A$ are algebra homomorphisms for the Koszul multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{|b||c|}ac\otimes bd$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}M_j$ be a coaugmented coassociative counital graded $k$-coalgebra with $M_0=ku$, $\varepsilon_M(u)=1$, and $\Delta_M(u)=u\otimes u$. Supply a $k$-bilinear unital left $A$-action satisfying $(ab)m=a(bm)$, $(\lambda1_A)m=\lambda m$, and $A_iM_j\subseteq M_{i+j}$. Give $M\otimes M$ the diagonal action $a(v\otimes w)=\sum(-1)^{|a_2||v|}(a_1v)\otimes(a_2w)$ for $\Delta_Aa=\sum a_1\otimes a_2$, and assume $\Delta_M(am)=a\Delta_M(m)$. If $\nu:A\to M$, $a\mapsto au$, is injective, set $A^+=\bigoplus_{i>0}A_i$ and $Q=M/A^+M$. Then $Q$ is nonnegatively graded with $Q_0=k\pi(u)$, and every graded $k$-linear section $f:Q\to M$ of $\pi$ induces a graded left $A$-module isomorphism $\Phi:A\otimes_kQ\to M$, $a\otimes q\mapsto af(q)$, with $A$ acting on the first tensor factor. Such a section exists under AC. Any homogeneous $k$-basis of $Q$ lifts under $f$ to a homogeneous free $A$-basis of $M$. No commutativity, antipode, or finite-type hypothesis is imposed; supplying the homogeneous basis and lifts removes additional choice from the proof.
entry.strategy: Use the stated grading/action axioms as local definitions; no later graded-algebra page is needed. The Koszul tensor formula is well defined by tensor universality, and its associativity follows by comparing the signs $|b_2||v|+|a_2|(|b_1|+|v|)$ and $|a_2||b_1|+(|a_2|+|b_2|)|v|$. Grading and the counits give $\Delta_M(m)=u\otimes m+m\otimes u+$ lower bidegrees for positive-degree $m$, while degree zero has the single term $\Delta_M(\lambda u)=\lambda u\otimes u$. The graded submodule $A^+M$ has no degree-zero part, and $\pi(am)=\varepsilon_A(a)\pi(m)$. Choose degree-preserving lifts of homogeneous bases to construct $f$. Prove surjectivity of $\Phi$ by degree induction: $m-f\pi(m)$ is a finite sum of positive-degree $A$-multiples of lower-degree vectors. For injectivity put $T=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\pi)\Delta_M$. Compatibility and the counit show $T(am)=aT(m)$ because terms with positive-degree second coproduct factor are killed by $\pi$. For homogeneous $q$ of degree $d$, $T\Phi(a\otimes q)=\nu(a)\otimes q+$ terms of second degree less than $d$, including the separate $d=0$ case. Write a putative kernel vector as a finite sum $\sum a_j\otimes q_j$ in a homogeneous basis of $Q$ and select its largest second degree. Projection there and the coordinate functionals force $\nu(a_j)=0$, hence $a_j=0$, a contradiction. Tensor/direct-sum and unit isomorphisms identify $A\otimes Q$ with a direct sum of copies of the potentially noncommutative ring $A$, yielding the claimed free basis.

entry.title: Finite-cover transfer with inverted degree and sign anti-invariants
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let p:Y→X be a nonempty finite d-sheeted regular cover of path-connected CW spaces, and let R be a commutative unital ring in which d is invertible. Pullback identifies H*(X;R) with the deck-invariant graded subalgebra H*(Y;R)^G. For a double cover and 2 invertible, let O_R be its associated sign local system. Then H*(X;O_R) is naturally the anti-invariant part of H*(Y;R). No finite-dimensionality hypothesis is imposed.
entry.strategy: Sum all lifts of each singular simplex to obtain the integral chain transfer τ; face restriction bijects lift sets, so τ commutes with boundary. On R-valued cochains the identities Tp*=d·id and p*T=Σg* prove injectivity and the invariant-image assertion. Identify sign-local-system cochains with anti-invariant cochains upstairs by signed lift coordinates and face transport. The cochain idempotents (1±σ*)/2 split the complex and therefore split cohomology. Ring identification comes from pullback multiplicativity, not transfer multiplicativity.

entry.title: Integral homology comparison gives finite-range homotopy comparison for simply connected CW complexes
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let N≥2 and let f:(X,x₀)→(Y,y₀) be a based continuous map between nonempty path-connected simply connected CW complexes. Suppose f_*:H_i(X;Z)→H_i(Y;Z) is an isomorphism for 0≤i<N and a surjection for i=N. Then f_*:π_i(X,x₀)→π_i(Y,y₀) is an isomorphism for 1≤i<N and a surjection for i=N. No conclusion about π_{N+1} or homotopy equivalence of the spaces is included.

Form its genuine CW mapping cylinder M with source subcomplex X and target deformation retraction. The relative homology exact sequence forces H_i(M,X;Z)=0 through N. Simple connectivity gives relative π₁=*. Induct on m=2,…,N: lower relative homotopy vanishing makes the CW pair (m−1)-connected, and relative Hurewicz identifies π_m(M,X) with the zero H_m(M,X). The relative homotopy exact sequence gives isomorphisms on π_i below N and surjectivity at N. Retract to Y and undo basepoint transport.

entry.title: Rationalization is exact and commutes with singular homology
entry.statement: Assume AC. For every abelian group A, A⊗_Z Q is its positive-integer localization: every element is a/s and a/s=0 iff a is killed by some positive integer. Thus A⊗Q=0 iff A is torsion. Rationalization is exact and commutes with direct sums. Naturally for every space Y, H_j(Y;Z)⊗Q≅H_j(Y;Q); for every rational vector space V, H_j(Y;V)≅H_j(Y;Q)⊗_Q V.
entry.strategy: Apply exact module localization and its tensor identification to the cycle/boundary short exact sequences of the singular chain complex. Clear denominators to obtain the torsion criterion. A basis of V identifies tensoring a rational complex with V with a direct sum; finite-support coordinate kernels and images give the natural coefficient comparison.

entry.title: Weak-join classifying model of a discrete group
entry.statement:
For a discrete group G, let J(G) be the weak geometric realization of the abstract simplicial complex with vertices (s,g), s∈N and g∈G, whose nonempty simplices contain at most one vertex in each slot s; include the empty simplex. Right multiplication on every label defines a G-action. Define B_wG=J(G)/G with the orbit quotient topology. Its geometric realization uses the published simplex-wise weak topology, not an alternative Milnor-model topology.

The construction is unambiguous: the vertex set and the simplex condition are defined by comprehension, and right multiplication $(s,h)\cdot g=(s,hg)$ preserves slot distinctness, so it is an automorphism of the abstract simplicial complex and restricts to a homeomorphism of the geometric realization. The orbit quotient and its quotient topology are therefore well defined as an ordinary quotient space, and the quotient map is continuous by definition of the quotient topology. The definition selects nothing; orbit representatives are needed only in later arguments and are handled there. The weak (simplex-wise) topology is the one fixed by [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]], not an alternative join-model topology.
entry.strategy: Define the downward-closed simplex family and its published weak realization; label translation preserves slots and faces, so gives a continuous action, with the CW and covering properties justified in the following lemma.

entry.title: Oriented Grassmannians have two lifted Schubert cells
entry.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. For n≥1, the forgetful map Gr⁺_n(R∞)=BSO(n)→Gr_n(R∞)=BO(n) is a two-sheeted cover, including n=1, where it is S∞→RP∞. Each Schubert cell has exactly two lifted cells, and these cells give BSO(n) the CW weak topology with finite boundary support. Set BSO(0) to the point.

Finite skeleta are compact Hausdorff finite attaching quotients. Check the infinite closed-set topology against the base weak-topology test on evenly covered charts, proving the lifted cells give precisely the CW weak topology.

entry.title: Adem reduction spans by admissible square composites
entry.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. In degree $N\ge0$, every element of $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ is a finite linear combination of the admissible words $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$ with $|I|=N$. Consequently the same is true in $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$.
entry.strategy: In degree N pad normalized positive sequences with terminal zeros to length N and order the finite set lexicographically. Each Adem replacement of a nonadmissible adjacent pair (a,b) replaces it by (a+b-j,j) with j<b, so its first changed entry strictly increases. Removing a terminal identity after that entry preserves the increase. Descending induction on this finite order terminates in admissible words, preserving total degree. The unit handles degree zero. Pass through the quotient-to-operation map to obtain the operation spanning assertion without assuming independence.

entry.title: Admissible square actions have distinct leading monomials
entry.statement:
Assume AC. Let $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ be admissible, let $r\ge e(I)$, and choose $L\ge |I|+1$. On

$$X=(\mathbb{RP}^{L})^r, \qquad H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)= \mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^{L+1},\ldots,x_r^{L+1}),$$

put $P=x_1\cdots x_r$. Order monomials lexicographically by their exponent vectors, largest first. The largest monomial of $Sq^I(P)$ has coefficient one and has exponents

$$(\underbrace{2^k,\ldots,2^k}_{d_k}, \underbrace{2^{k-1},\ldots,2^{k-1}}_{d_{k-1}}, \ldots, \underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{d_1}, \underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-e(I)}).$$

For fixed total degree $|I|$, different admissible sequences have different largest monomials. The empty sequence gives $P$.
entry.strategy: Compute finite projective-space cohomology and its product ring using the published cellular and finite-free Künneth interfaces. Cartan and the top-square identity give Sq^a(x^m)=binom(m,a)x^(m+a); for m a power of two the only possible actions are no change or doubling. Regard each composite as a finite schedule of doublings. For a sequence of length k, at most i_k variables can reach exponent 2^k; reaching that maximum forces their complete doubling chains. Subtract their forced costs from the earlier budgets and induct on the residual admissible sequence. This proves both maximality and coefficient one, with multiplicities d_k,…,d_1. The exponent bound 1+|I| prevents truncation; backward recursion recovers I from these multiplicities. Distinct leading terms, rather than disjoint supports, prove the asserted distinction.

entry.title: The fundamental path-fibration class has the normalized relative lift
entry.statement:
Assume AC. For $n\ge1$, in the marked path fibration $F=\Omega K_{n+1}\to P K_{n+1}\xrightarrow p K_{n+1}$, with the fiber identified in marked homology and cohomology with $K_n$ by the weak equivalence of Item 6,

\[
 \delta\iota_n=p^*\iota_{n+1}
 \quad\text{in }H^{n+1}(P K_{n+1},F;\mathbb F_2).
\]
entry.strategy: Represent the marked nonzero fiber homotopy class by a based sphere map. Its Hurewicz image is the nonzero integral homology generator: transfer ordinary CW Hurewicz through Item 6's weak equivalence for n>1, and use abelianization for n=1. Nullhomotope the sphere in the contractible path space to a disk lift A. Its finite disk fundamental chain defines a relative generator z, whose pair-LES boundary is the marked fiber generator. The collapsed projected disk represents the marked base homotopy class by the fibration connecting map. The good-pair quotient and natural cellular comparison identify p_*z with its base Hurewicz image. Verify the relative, base and fiber UCT Ext terms vanish, explicitly using connected H_0 for n=1. Both the connector and pulled-back fundamental class evaluate as one on z, so relative evaluation UCT identifies them. No relative Hurewicz theorem or fiber homotopy-equivalence premise is used.

entry.title: Relative lifts produce cohomological transgressions
entry.statement:
Assume AC. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Serre fibration over a simply connected CW base with basepoint vertex and fiber $F$. If $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$, $m>0$, and $y\in H^{m+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy

\[
 \delta x=p^*y\quad\text{in }H^{m+1}(E,F;\mathbb F_2),
\]

then $x$ survives to $E_{m+1}^{0,m}$ and its differential $d_{m+1}$ is the bottom-axis coset represented by $y$. Moreover $Sq^a x$ has the same property with representative $Sq^a y$ at page $m+a+1$, whenever its degree is positive.
entry.strategy: Lift the base class y to cohomology relative to the m-skeleton, using cellular vanishing and the pair LES. Choose its cocycle v vanishing on that skeleton. Extend a representative of x to E and correct it by a cochain vanishing on F so that its coboundary is exactly p^*v. This lies in skeletal filtration m+1, giving survival to that page and the specified bottom-axis coset differential by the filtered page formulas and Serre base-edge construction. Connector compatibility and relative square naturality give the analogous relative lift for Sq^a x; repeat the same argument in its new total degree. No unproved operation on spectral-sequence pages is assumed.

entry.title: Finite type and odd-primary acyclicity of K(F₂,q)
entry.statement: Assume AC. For every q≥1 and every CW model K_q=K(Z/2,q), H_n(K_q;Z) is finitely generated for every n; for n>0 it is a finite 2-primary group. For every field F of characteristic different from two, H_n(K_q;F)=H^n(K_q;F)=0 for n>0 and H_0=H^0=F. The F₂ homology and cohomology are finite-dimensional degreewise, with H^i=0 for 0<i<q and H^q=F₂ with its normalized fundamental class. Positive integral cohomology is finite 2-primary. These are homological finite-type assertions, not finite-cell claims about arbitrary CW models.
entry.strategy: Use the marked RP∞ model and its one-cell-per-degree Schubert structure for q=1; transfer from its contractible antipodal cover gives away-from-two field acyclicity. Induct via the actual contractible path fibration over K_q, comparing its strict loop fiber to K_{q−1} by weak CW approximation, marked EM uniqueness and weak-map homology invariance. In the integral homological Serre sequence, prove finite generation of the bottom-row group H_s(K_q;Z) by induction on s: it has no incoming differential, all finitely many outgoing targets are subquotients of lower-base-degree coefficient homology and are finitely generated by UCT and Noetherianity, and its terminal kernel is zero. For fields away from two the fiber has only H_0, so the contractible abutment forces base acyclicity. UCT and finite abelian-group decomposition then give finite 2-primary homology and the remaining coefficient assertions.

entry.title: Finite-range comparison with an arbitrary simply connected target
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let N≥2, X be a nonempty path-connected simply connected CW complex, Y an arbitrary nonempty path-connected simply connected space, and f:(X,x₀)→(Y,y₀) a based continuous map. If its integral homology maps are isomorphisms for 0≤i<N and surjective at N, its based homotopy maps are isomorphisms for 1≤i<N and surjective at N. Its component and homotopy isomorphisms make Z path-connected and simply connected; weak-map integral homology invariance gives homology isomorphisms for Q. Therefore the inclusion j:X→Z inherits f’s precise homology hypotheses from Q_*j_*=f_*. Apply the CW comparison theorem to j and compose with Q_* on based homotopy groups. entry.title: Rational cohomology of K(Z,n) through weak CW fiber comparison
entry.statement: Assume AC. For each marked CW K(Z,n), n≥1, rational cohomology is Q[x_n] when n is even and Λ_Q(x_n) when n is odd, with |x_n|=n and x_n dual to the marked generator. In particular positive rational homology below 2n vanishes except for the one-dimensional group in degree n.
entry.strategy: Weakly approximate the strict loop fiber and identify that CW approximation with the marked K(Z,n−1); the actual weak-equivalence map gives a rational cohomology ring isomorphism by homology comparison and field duality. Start with S^1. In the multiplicative path-fibration Serre sequence, an exterior fiber generator transgresses to x and multiplication by x is bijective in the necessary degrees, giving the even polynomial case. entry.title: Cohomology of BO and BSO away from two
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let R be a nonzero commutative unital ring with 2 invertible. For m≥1, H*(BSO(2m+1);R)=R[p₁,…,p_m], H*(BSO(2m);R)=R[p₁,…,p_{m−1},e] with p_m=e², and H*(BO(2m);R)=H*(BO(2m+1);R)=R[p₁,…,p_m]. At odd rank the two-torsion Euler class vanishes over R, so restriction is injective. The sphere-vector involution reverses the even-dimensional complement orientation, forcing its image into the even Euler powers, already attained by the Pontryagin generators. entry.title: The Thom prespectrum of the universal real and oriented bundles
entry.statement: Assume AC, as inherited from the published bundle-classification suppliers. Let $\gamma_r\to B\mathrm O(r)$ and $\gamma_r^{+}\to B\mathrm{SO}(r)$ be the universal metric rank-$r$ bundles in the published Grassmannian models. For $r\ge0$ set $M\mathrm O_r=\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_r)$ and $M\mathrm{SO}_r=\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_r^{+})$, with the based rank-zero convention of the published Thom-space definition. Let $J(x_1,x_2,\ldots)=(0,x_1,x_2,\ldots)$. Fix $\iota_r(W)=\mathbb R e_1\oplus J(W)$ and its oriented version $(W,o)\mapsto(\mathbb R e_1\oplus J(W),e_1\wedge J_*o)$, the Grassmannian stabilization $\iota_r$ which adds the specified trivial coordinate line, with its fiberwise isometric identification $\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r\cong\iota_r^*\gamma_{r+1}$; use $\varepsilon^1_+\oplus\gamma_r^+$ in the same first-coordinate order for its orientation-preserving counterpart. Define the structure map by the composite $S^1\wedge M\mathrm O_r\cong\mathrm{Th}(\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r)\cong\mathrm{Th}(\iota_r^*\gamma_{r+1})\longrightarrow\mathrm{Th}(\gamma_{r+1})=M\mathrm O_{r+1}$, where the final arrow is induced by the pullback bundle projection covering $\iota_r$; the sphere coordinate is placed first as in the published prespectrum convention. The analogous maps define $M\mathrm{SO}$. Write $T_r=M\mathrm O_r$, $T_r^+=M\mathrm{SO}_r$, $s_r=\iota_r$ and $s_r^+=\iota_r^+$, and denote the structure maps by $\alpha_r$ and $\alpha_r^+$. These supplied spaces and structure maps are the two sequential Thom prespectra used here. Their stable homotopy groups are $\pi_n(M\mathrm O)=\operatorname{colim}_{r}\pi_{n+r}(M\mathrm O_r)$ and $\pi_n(M\mathrm{SO})=\operatorname{colim}_{r}\pi_{n+r}(M\mathrm{SO}_r)$, with transition maps given by suspension followed by the structure map. Only these two prespectra are used; no general Thom-spectrum theory is developed here. For each fixed n, the displayed colimit is taken over a tail r≥r₀ with r+n≥1, exactly as in [[def-stable-homotopy-groups-of-a-sequential-prespectrum]].
entry.strategy: Use the fixed-coordinate embeddings iota_r(W)=R e_1⊕J(W). On each finite Stiefel stage the frame formula (v_1,…,v_r)↦(e_1,Jv_1,…,Jv_r) is continuous and equivariant for the block inclusion O(r)→O(r+1), so it descends through the Grassmannian quotient and its weak direct-limit topology. The fiber map (t,v)↦t e_1+Jv is an isometry ε¹⊕γ_r→iota_r^*γ_{r+1}; for the oriented bundles use the same construction with orientation e_1∧J_*o and the block inclusion SO(r)→SO(r+1). The local two-sheeted-cover lemma supplies the lifted BSO Schubert CW structure; rank zero is the point with its positive line. The disk/sphere quotient and trivial-line Thom identification give the based homeomorphism S¹∧Th(γ_r)≅Th(ε¹⊕γ_r), with the sphere coordinate first. Compose this homeomorphism, the displayed bundle isometry, and the Thom map of the actual pullback-bundle projection to Th(γ_{r+1}). That projection preserves the disk and sphere subspaces, so the quotient universal property makes the structure map based and continuous; the same argument applies to MSO. For the level topology, trivialize the pulled-back bundle over each Schubert characteristic disk. The disk/sphere quotient contributes one cell of dimension d+r over each d-cell, attached along the base boundary and fiber sphere. The finite-stage attaching quotients have their stated topology by the compact-to-Hausdorff quotient test. For the infinite disk bundle, every compact Hausdorff test map projects to a compact subset of the base and hence, by the cited compact-image result, lies over a finite Schubert subcomplex. It factors through the corresponding finite disk-bundle stage. The characteristic-disk tests therefore give the weak attachment topology; the quotient map test gives the same weak topology on the Thom space. The finite-boundary attachment lemma proves that this weak cell topology is Hausdorff and closure-finite. A subset is closed exactly when its inverse image in every compact characteristic ball is closed, so the compact-test characterization proves compact generation. Every compact Hausdorff test image is compact in this Hausdorff CW space and hence closed by the compact-subset theorem; this proves weak Hausdorffness. The basepoint is a CW vertex, and the relative-CW cofibration result makes its inclusion a cofibration. Thus every level is a well-pointed based CGWH CW space, as required by the sequential-prespectrum definition. Rank zero is separately S⁰. The stable-homotopy-group definition then supplies the stated colimits over admissible cofinal tails. These are explicit fixed maps, not maps identified only up to arbitrary classifying homotopy; no Omega-prespectrum condition or general represented-spectrum comparison is asserted.

entry.title: Admissible composites present the mod-two square algebra
entry.statement: Assume AC. The natural map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is an isomorphism. In each degree $N$, its admissible composites $Sq^I$ with $|I|=N$ form an $\mathbb F_2$-basis. For a putative nonzero homogeneous relation of degree N among their natural operations, evaluate every term on the same product class on (RP^(N+1))^(N+1). The leading-monomial lemma applies to every sequence. Its largest occurring leading monomial cannot cancel against terms with smaller leading monomials, so the relation is nonzero. The identity is nonzero in degree zero. Since the quotient relations are homogeneous, degreewise independence makes the already surjective quotient-to-operation map injective.

entry.title: A transgressive simple fiber system gives a polynomial base
entry.statement:
Assume AC. Let $F\to E\to B$ be a Serre fibration with $E$ contractible and $B$ simply connected CW. The hypotheses concern the actual strict fiber cohomology ring; no CW-type or homotopy-equivalence assertion for the fiber is assumed. Suppose $H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)$ has a basis consisting of the finite products of **distinct** positive-degree classes $x_\lambda$, including the empty product, and only finitely many $x_\lambda$ occur in each degree. Suppose classes $y_\lambda\in H^{|x_\lambda|+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy $\delta x_\lambda=p^*y_\lambda$. Then

$$\mathbb F_2[Y_\lambda]\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(B;\mathbb F_2), \qquad Y_\lambda\longmapsto y_\lambda.$$

No assertion that $x_\lambda^2=0$ is required.
entry.strategy: Build a model spectral sequence for each simple fiber generator with exterior x and polynomial Y, whose only differential is xY^a↦Y^(a+1) on page |x|+1. Tensor these factor sequences degreewise. Published vector-space bases and AC split complexes into homology plus contractible pairs; the tensor universal property, tensor/direct-sum and tensor-unit interfaces give the page-homology comparison, and H⊗id contracts each tensor pair. Positive degrees and local finiteness ensure only finitely many factors contribute per total degree. Evaluate squarefree fiber monomials and polynomial base monomials on the actual classes. Relative lifts and Leibniz give a morphism on every page; it is additive, not necessarily multiplicative in the fiber direction. The fiber axis and limiting scalar pages are isomorphic. Item 7d therefore identifies the base E_2 axis; there the map is the asserted polynomial ring homomorphism. Only computed strict-fiber cohomology is required.

entry.title: Finite products and comparison cones have homological finite type
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let Y be a finite product of CW K(Z/2,q) models with q≥1, including the empty product *. Then every H_n(Y;Z) is finitely generated and H^*(Y;F)=F in degree zero only for every field F of characteristic different from two. entry.title: Degreewise mod-two cohomology of the universal real Thom prespectrum
entry.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the shared bundle and Thom construction. Use the real levels $T_r=\operatorname{Th}(\gamma_r)$ and first-coordinate structure maps $\alpha_r:S^1\wedge T_r\to T_{r+1}$ of the shared Thom prespectrum. For $q\in\mathbb Z$ put $A_r(q)=\widetilde H^{r+q}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$ and define the backwards bonding map

$$\rho_r(q)=\sigma^{-1}\alpha_r^*:A_{r+1}(q)\longrightarrow A_r(q),$$

where $\sigma$ is reduced cohomology suspension with the sphere coordinate first. Define

$$\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)=\{(x_r)_{r\ge0}\in\prod_{r\ge0}A_r(q):\rho_r(q)x_{r+1}=x_r\text{ for every }r\},\qquad \widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbb Z}\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2).$$

The conditions are linear, so this is a well-defined vector space with componentwise operations. It is an inverse-limit prespectrum invariant; identifying it with represented spectrum cohomology would require a separate comparison theorem.

The normalized Thom isomorphisms give $A_r(q)\cong H^q(BO(r);\mathbb F_2)$, with $u_r$ the normalized rank-$r$ Thom class. The bonding-map computation and eventual constancy are proved in [[lem-stable-thom-cohomology-is-degreewise-eventually-constant]]: all terms vanish for $q<0$, and for $q\ge0$ projection to any rank $r\ge q$ identifies the compatible tuples with the weight-$q$ polynomial Thom module. In particular, writing $U=(u_r)$,

$$\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]U,\qquad |w_i|=i,\quad |U|=0.$$

This is a graded vector-space and characteristic-polynomial-module identification, justified by that lemma. It gives no ring structure from reduced finite-level cup products. Each weight is finite-dimensional.
entry.strategy: The shared prespectrum supplies the based continuous maps and the fixed order of the suspension coordinate. The CW and suspension-normalization proof within the moved shared combined prespectrum definition identifies suspension of each Thom-module class with the class of the bundle after adding the first trivial line; the two Thom isomorphisms and the natural relative/reduced quotient comparison make that suspension an isomorphism in every required degree. Pullback followed by its inverse therefore has exactly the stated domain and codomain and is linear. The compatibility equations define a linear subspace of the product, since each bonding map is linear; componentwise addition and scalar multiplication preserve them. The direct sum over $q$ imposes finite grading support rather than a completion. The following eventual-constancy lemma separately justifies the resulting invariant and its computation; no general inverse-limit theorem is used.

is injective. If $f:X\to K_q$ classifies $z\in\widetilde H^q(X;\mathbb F_2)$, then $f^*\eta_{q,i}(a)=a(z)$.

entry.title: Finite-generation cohomological UCT gives integral cone comparison
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let D≥0 and let C be a nonnegative free integral chain complex whose H_i(C) are finitely generated for 0≤i≤D. If H^i(Hom_Z(C,Q))=0 and H^i(Hom_Z(C,F_p))=0 for every prime p in those degrees, then H_i(C)=0 for 0≤i≤D. Consequently, for a continuous map f:X→Y with degreewise finitely generated integral homology, field cohomology isomorphisms f*:H^i(Y;F)→H^i(X;F) for F=Q and every F_p and 0≤i≤D imply integral homology isomorphisms f_* for i<D and surjectivity for i=D. No degree-D injectivity or degree-D+1 field hypothesis is asserted.
entry.strategy: Cohomological UCT surjects each zero field cohomology group onto Hom(H_i(C),F). Finite abelian-group decomposition shows that Q detects any nonzero free summand and F_p detects any nonzero p-primary summand, so H_i(C)=0. For C=Cone(C_*(f;Z)), use the cone finite-generation lemma and dualize the degreewise split cone sequence. entry.title: Stable universal Thom cohomology is eventually constant in every degree
entry.statement: Assume AC through the published Thom and universal-bundle suppliers. For the preceding compatible-tuple invariant, the normalized Thom isomorphisms identify $\rho_r(q)$ with the homogeneous-weight-$q$ map $\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_{r+1}]^q\to\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_r]^q$ sending $w_i$ to $w_i$ for $i\le r$ and $w_{r+1}$ to zero. If $q<0$ all terms are zero. If $q\ge0$, every bonding map with $r\ge q$ is an isomorphism, and projection to any level $r\ge q$ identifies $\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)$ with $\mathbb F_2[w_1,\ldots,w_r]^q u_r$. Writing $U=(u_r)$, this gives $\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]U$, with $|w_i|=i$ and $|U|=0$, as a graded vector space and as a module over the stable characteristic polynomial algebra. Each homogeneous piece is finite-dimensional. The assertion is a Thom-module computation, not an identification of reduced cup rings or a general spectrum-comparison theorem.
entry.strategy: Let $\Phi_r(a)=a u_r$. The specified first-coordinate stabilization pulls back $\gamma_{r+1}$ to $\varepsilon^1\oplus\gamma_r$. Thom pullback naturality and the suspension normalization proved within that moved shared definition give $\alpha_r^*\Phi_{r+1}(a)=\sigma\Phi_r(s_r^*a)$, so $\Phi_r^{-1}\rho_r\Phi_{r+1}=s_r^*$. Stiefel–Whitney naturality, the Whitney formula, and trivial-line normalization identify $s_r^*w_i$ with $w_i$ below the old rank and with zero above it. Apply the published $BO(r)$ polynomial theorem. No weight-$q$ monomial contains a variable of weight exceeding $q$, so the map is bijective for $r\ge q$. A value at any such tail level extends uniquely to later levels by inverse bonding isomorphisms and to earlier levels by the original bonding maps; this gives the stated compatible-tuple computation without a general spectral comparison. The Thom-class normalization proves compatibility of $U$. Characteristic polynomials act componentwise after restriction to each rank, giving the claimed graded module. In weight $q$, only variables $w_i$ with $i\le q$ can appear, and each exponent is at most $q/i$, so there are finitely many monomials. Negative weights vanish by the Thom isomorphism. Rank zero and degree zero use $T_0=S^0$ and its normalized reduced Thom class.

entry.title: The admissible square algebra is a connected bialgebra

Multiplicativity and the fact that this kernel is a two-sided ideal extend the coideal condition to the full Adem ideal; positive-degree generators also force the counit to vanish on that ideal. entry.title: Metastable cohomology of mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
entry.statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$ and $0\le i<q$, evaluation on the normalized mod-two fundamental class is an isomorphism

\[

\]

Evaluation therefore takes the admissible operation basis bijectively to this cohomology basis. Item 5 also gives independent injectivity. entry.title: Stable Steenrod squares on universal Thom cohomology
entry.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. For $i\ge0$ and $x=(x_r)\in\widehat H^q(TO;\mathbb F_2)$, define $Sq^i x$ by the components $(Sq^i x)_r=Sq^i(x_r)$ in $\widetilde H^{r+q+i}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$. At a negative finite-level source degree use the unique map from the zero cohomology group. These components form a compatible tuple, giving a linear map $Sq^i:\widehat H^q\to\widehat H^{q+i}$. For the stable normalized Thom vector $U$, $Sq^iU=w_iU$ with $w_0=1$; its rank-$r$ component is zero for $i>r$. The degree-zero stable vector $U$ is not subject to the instability bound for a degree-zero class of a space: its rank-$r$ representative has degree $r$. No freeness or homotopy-detection conclusion is asserted here.
entry.strategy: Pullback naturality commutes each square with $\alpha_r^*$, and the published reduced suspension identity commutes it with $\sigma$ and $\sigma^{-1}$. Thus $\rho_r(q+i)Sq^i=Sq^i\rho_r(q)$, proving compatibility and linearity. Normalization and Adem identities hold at every finite level, hence on the tuples and their graded direct sum. The Thom identity gives $Sq^i u_r=w_i(\gamma_r)u_r$, including rank zero and the vanishing for $i>r$. Under the preceding eventual-constancy/polynomial-module identification these are exactly the components of $w_iU$. All stable-degree claims are checked through the actual level degrees $r+q$; no finite-level instability rule is incorrectly imposed at stable degree $q$.

entry.title: Whitney-sum coalgebra on stable unoriented Thom cohomology
entry.statement:
Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Let $\mathcal P=\mathbb F_2[w_1,w_2,\ldots]$ with $|w_k|=k$, and use the graded identification $M=\mathcal P U$ with $|U|=0$ and $w_0=1$. Extend $\Delta_P(w_k)=\sum_{i+j=k}w_i\otimes w_j$ uniquely to a unital algebra homomorphism $\Delta_P:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal P$. Define the candidate maps $\Delta_M(fU)=\Delta_P(f)(U\otimes U)$, $\epsilon_M(fU)=f(0)$, and $\eta(1)=U$. These formulas specify the proposed Whitney-sum operations; their well-definedness, inverse-limit compatibility, and coalgebra axioms are proved in [[lem-whitney-sum-coalgebra-is-well-defined-on-stable-thom-cohomology]].


Each polynomial has finite support and each generator coproduct is a finite sum, so these are degree-preserving linear maps on $M$ and the ordinary graded tensor product. The rankwise geometric interpretation is the Thom pullback of an external Whitney sum, with

$$w_kU\longmapsto\sum_{i+j=k}(w_iU)\otimes(w_jU),\qquad U\longmapsto U\otimes U.$$

The cited well-definedness lemma proves agreement with that geometric pullback, stabilization compatibility, coassociativity, and both counit identities; these are obligations of the construction rather than additional premises.
entry.strategy: This item fixes the polynomial formulas and the coaugmentation. The following local lemma constructs the rankwise Whitney-sum pullbacks, verifies their compatibility with both fixed-coordinate bonding systems using the external Thom product and relative field Künneth, and proves the counit and coassociativity identities. No represented-spectrum cohomology comparison is used.

entry.title: Whitney sum defines the connected coalgebra on stable Thom cohomology
entry.statement: Assume AC, inherited from the cited bundle, cohomology, or operation suppliers. Assume the displayed identification M=F₂[w₁,w₂,…]U and the formulas of [[def-whitney-sum-coalgebra-on-stable-unoriented-thom-cohomology]]. Then Δ_M:M→M⊗M is a degree-preserving coassociative coproduct, ε_M is a counit, and η(1)=U is a coaugmentation. M is connected and nonnegatively graded. For each p,q, the rankwise Thom pullback induced by γ_p⊕γ_q agrees with Δ_M under the Thom isomorphisms, commutes with the fixed-coordinate stabilization in each factor, and therefore induces the stated map on the degreewise inverse-limit invariant.

On the polynomial generators both iterated coproducts send w_k to the sum over i+j+ℓ=k, while Δ_M(U)=U⊗U, so coassociativity extends multiplicatively. entry.title: Finite Thom classifying detector map
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathcal A$ be the mod-two square algebra acting on $M=\widehat H^*(TO;\mathbb F_2)$, let $\mathcal A^+=\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathcal A^j$ be its positive-degree ideal, and put $Q=M/\mathcal A^+M$ as in the freeness theorem. Fix once and for all a homogeneous basis $B=\coprod_{d\ge0}B_d$ of $Q$ and a degree-preserving section $s:Q\to M$ of the quotient map, using AC; these choices are shared by every rank. For $b\in B_d$ set $m_b=s(b)$ and $d_b=d$. For each $r\ge2$, set $B(r)=\bigcup_{0\le d<r}B_d$. The freeness theorem makes all $m_b$, for $b\in B$, a homogeneous free $\mathcal A$-basis of $M$. Via the eventual-constancy isomorphism $M^d\cong\widetilde H^{r+d}(T_r;\mathbb F_2)$, let $\bar m_{b,r}$ be the rank-r coordinate of the same fixed $m_b$, and choose a based representative $f_{r,b}:T_r\to K(\mathbb F_2,r+d_b)$ of its representing class. Set $P_r=\prod_{b\in B(r)}K(\mathbb F_2,r+d_b)$ and define the candidate based detector $f_r:T_r\to P_r$ by its coordinate maps. The same basis and lifts are used at every rank, so the coordinates are compatible with prespectrum stabilization. The finite existence and continuity argument is recorded in [[lem-finite-thom-classifying-detector-map-exists-and-is-continuous]].

Reuse the same lifts m_b=s(b) at every rank, and for rank r use only the finite initial segment B(r)=⋃_{d<r}B_d. The freeness theorem makes all lifts a free A-basis; finite-dimensional degree pieces make B(r) finite. Eventual constancy supplies the rank-r classes, Eilenberg–Mac Lane representability supplies based coordinate maps, and the finite-product universal property assembles f_r. This global choice is the one used in the suspension-compatibility lemma.

entry.statement: Assume AC. Fix n≥0 and V_n=F₂^{B_n}. For every r≥n+2 let D_{r,n}:π_{r+n}(T_r)→V_n pair a sphere class with the rank-r stable-coordinate classes m_{r,b}, b∈B_n. entry.title: Exotic smooth structure and exotic sphere
entry.statement: A smooth manifold $X$ is an exotic smooth structure on a specified smooth manifold $Y$ when their underlying topological manifolds are homeomorphic and $X$ is not diffeomorphic to $Y$. An exotic smooth $n$-sphere is a closed connected smooth $n$-manifold homeomorphic, but not diffeomorphic, to the standard smooth $S^n$. An orientation is extra data when oriented classes are compared. This definition concerns the smooth category; a homotopy equivalence alone does not assert a homeomorphism.
entry.strategy: The homeomorphism and diffeomorphism predicates fix the two categories. The exoticness assertion is proved below for concrete seven-spheres.

entry.title: Smooth homotopy sphere
entry.statement: A smooth homotopy $n$-sphere is a closed connected smooth $n$-manifold $Σ$ equipped with a homotopy equivalence $Σ\simeq S^n$. An oriented homotopy sphere carries a chosen orientation. No topological Poincaré assertion is built into the definition.

entry.title: Compact smooth manifolds have finite CW models under countable choice
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every compact smooth manifold, with boundary allowed, has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex. If its boundary is a supplied finite CW manifold, its collar may be retained in a finite relative CW model.
entry.strategy: Assume ACω for collars, partitions and the handle-to-cell interfaces. Regard W as the collared triad (W;empty,∂W); for a closed W both faces are empty. Construct a smooth boundary-product function f0 from the collar and a partition of unity. Its differential is nonzero on a fixed boundary strip. Cover the compact complement of a smaller strip by finitely many coordinate charts with smaller compactly contained chart cores and bumps ρ_i equal to one near those cores and supported away from the boundary. The finitely many functions ρ_i x_i^j have differentials spanning T*W at every point of this compact core. For the finite-dimensional family f_t=f0+Σt_ijρ_i x_i^j, the universal differential section is transverse to the zero section on the core. The zero set is a smooth parameterized critical-point manifold; applying the Euclidean Sard theorem in its countably many charts gives parameters t arbitrarily near zero for which the parameter projection is regular, equivalently every critical point of f_t is nondegenerate. ACω supplies at most countably many chart/null-cover choices; no infinite sequence of perturbations or general full-AC relative-jet theorem is used. Choose t small enough to keep df nonzero on the remaining boundary strip. Compactness makes the isolated critical set finite. Finite disjoint critical-point bumps separate its critical values while preserving the collar and nondegeneracy. This gives the adapted excellent Morse function actually needed by the ACω handle-correspondence statement; do not invoke its full-AC existence dependency. Its finite handle decomposition starts at the empty incoming face. Applying the declared handle-to-cell lemma successively gives a finite absolute CW model; with an already supplied finite incoming face the identical argument gives the relative version. Empty and zero-dimensional manifolds have finite discrete models. This finite-parameter construction is a local Step3 proof obligation, not an authored proof body.

entry.title: Connected sum preserves homotopy spheres
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge3$, the oriented connected sum of two oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres is again an oriented smooth homotopy $n$-sphere.
entry.strategy: Excising a disk from either summand preserves homology below degree $n-1$ and makes the punctured homotopy sphere acyclic, with the relative disk fundamental class mapping to its boundary fundamental class. Mayer–Vietoris for the two punctured manifolds joined along $S^{n-1}$ yields the integral homology of $S^n$; van Kampen gives trivial fundamental group. Collapse the complement of an oriented disk to obtain a degree-one map to $S^n$, hence a homology isomorphism. Finite CW models and the simply connected homology Whitehead theorem make this a homotopy equivalence. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness. The degree-one collapse from the connected sum to S^n is explicit; its homology equivalence is checked by the punctured-sphere Mayer–Vietoris calculation. No generator-selection use of the full-AC absolute Hurewicz theorem occurs here.

entry.title: Connected sum descends to oriented h-cobordism classes
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, oriented connected sum of smooth homotopy $n$-spheres descends to oriented h-cobordism classes and is associative and commutative, with the standard sphere as identity.
entry.strategy: Assume AC_omega. Given h-cobordisms W: Sigma_0 -> Sigma_1 and W': Sigma'_0 -> Sigma'_1, choose orientation-compatible small coordinate disks in each incoming and outgoing face, attach a product 1-handle in the incoming collars joining the two incoming faces and a second product 1-handle in the outgoing collars joining the two outgoing faces, and round the corners by smooth collar gluing; the resulting compact cobordism has ends Sigma_0#Sigma'_0 and Sigma_1#Sigma'_1. For each new end inclusion, the homotopy inverses of the two given face inclusions, chosen along the collar neighbourhoods to agree with the attaching identifications, extend over the 1-handles and glue with the collar flow to homotopy inverses, so both end inclusions are homotopy equivalences and the cobordism is an h-cobordism. Disk-choice independence and the interchange and regrouping of the collar-handle picture are obtained by isotoping the attaching data (centres joined by a path in the connected face with oriented frames transported; the finitely many disks already used can be avoided) and applying the local handle-isotopy lemma, whose later-handles clause transfers the diffeomorphism to the total cobordisms. Removing a disk from S^n leaves a disk, so S^n#Sigma is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to Sigma. This proves the stated laws without using the h-cobordism-to-diffeomorphism theorem.

entry.title: Orientation reversal is the connected-sum inverse
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, $\Sigma\#(-\Sigma)$ is oriented h-cobordant to $S^n$ for each oriented smooth homotopy $n$-sphere $\Sigma$.
entry.strategy: For n≥5 choose a smoothly embedded disk Dⁿ in Σ and set P=Σ\int(Dⁿ). The homology sequence of (Σ,P), excision to (Dⁿ,Sⁿ⁻¹), and van Kampen show P is acyclic and simply connected; the declared finite model and simply connected homology-Whitehead criterion give contractibility. This is the punctured homotopy sphere used in Kervaire–Milnor Lemma 2.4, not an assertion about arbitrary disk complements. Form V=P×[0,1]. Its corners along ∂P×{0,1} are rounded using product collars. The oriented boundary consists of P at the two ends joined by ∂P×[0,1], which is precisely Σ#(−Σ) with the second copy oppositely oriented; V is contractible. Remove the interior of a small smoothly embedded (n+1)-disk to obtain C, whose other boundary face is Sⁿ. Excision identifies H*(C,Sⁿ) with H*(V,Dⁿ⁺¹)=0, so Sⁿ→C is a homology isomorphism. The boundary fundamental-class relation [Σ#(−Σ)]+[Sⁿ]=0 in H_n(C) then shows the other boundary inclusion also induces an isomorphism (C has H_n=Z and no other reduced homology). Van Kampen applied after reattaching the removed disk shows π₁(C)=π₁(V)=0, since Sⁿ is simply connected; both faces are simply connected. The compact smooth CW models and Whitehead make both inclusions homotopy equivalences. Thus C is an h-cobordism from Sⁿ to Σ#(−Σ), proving that orientation reversal is the inverse. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness.

entry.title: The homotopy-sphere group Θ_n
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, let $\Theta_n$ be the set of oriented h-cobordism classes of oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres, with connected sum as addition, $[S^n]$ as zero, and $[-\Sigma]$ as the inverse of $[\Sigma]$. The preceding connected-sum and inverse lemmas establish that this is an abelian group.
entry.strategy: Under ACω, the connected-sum lemma proves the operation is well-defined and associative/commutative with identity, and the orientation-reversal lemma proves inverses. These verified laws give the stated abelian group structure.

entry.title: H-cobordism of homotopy spheres equals oriented diffeomorphism
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, two oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres are oriented h-cobordant if and only if they are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. Thus the underlying classes of $\Theta_n$ can be read as oriented diffeomorphism classes.
entry.strategy: An oriented diffeomorphism gives the product h-cobordism. Conversely an oriented h-cobordism has dimension $n+1\ge6$ and simply connected closed boundary faces, since each is a homotopy sphere. The smooth simply connected h-cobordism theorem, with its $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ premise, gives a product relative to one face; its other face is therefore oriented diffeomorphic to the first.

entry.title: Parallelizable bounds define a subgroup
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For n≥5, when Θₙ is the oriented homotopy-sphere group, its classes represented by boundaries of compact oriented parallelizable smooth (n+1)-manifolds form a subgroup.
entry.strategy: Assume ACω exactly for the h-cobordism-to-oriented-diffeomorphism theorem. First, if oriented homotopy spheres Σ and Σ′ represent the same Θₙ class, that theorem gives an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism f:Σ→Σ′. If Σ=∂V for a compact oriented parallelizable filling, transport its tangent trivialization along a collar and pull V across f; the resulting filling of Σ′ is still parallelizable. Thus the bounding property is independent of the chosen h-cobordism representative. If V and V′ are parallelizable oriented fillings, form their oriented boundary connected sum by attaching an (n+1)-dimensional 1-handle along small oriented n-disks in their boundaries and round the corners with collars. Its boundary is ∂V#∂V′. The given tangent frames restrict over the attaching disks; choose orientation-compatible disk frames and a path in GL⁺(n+1), which is connected, to match them to the product frame on the handle. The frames then glue to a global trivialization of the new tangent bundle, so the connected sum again bounds a parallelizable manifold. Finally −V is parallelizable with the reversed orientation and ∂(−V)=−∂V; by the preceding inverse lemma this boundary represents the additive inverse. The identity class bounds Dⁿ⁺¹. These establish representative independence, closure and inverse, hence the subgroup assertion.

entry.title: Quaternionic clutching bundles over S⁴
entry.statement: Identify the oriented fibre $\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb H$ in the ordered basis $(1,i,j,k)$ and $S^3$ with unit quaternions. Give $S^4=D^4_+\cup_{S^3}D^4_-$ the orientation whose equatorial clutching-degree convention sends $u\mapsto(v\mapsto uv)$ and $u\mapsto(v\mapsto vu)$ to Euler number $+1$; let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be its positive generator. For integers $h,j$, $\xi_{h,j}$ is the oriented real rank-four bundle obtained by $(a,v)_+\sim(a,g_{h,j}(a)v)_-$, $g_{h,j}(a)v=a^hva^j$. Unit quaternion multiplication makes this a smooth norm-preserving oriented clutching map for every integer exponent.
entry.strategy: Bundle existence and the upper-to-lower transition convention are supplied by clutching. The Euler-degree calibration and independence of the two basic maps are justified in subsequent local lemmas.

entry.title: Euler number from the clutching obstruction
entry.statement: Assume AC as inherited from the Euler-class supplier. For an oriented rank-four bundle over $S^4$ clutched by $g:S^3\to SO(4)$, evaluation of the Euler class on $[S^4]$ is the degree of $a\mapsto g(a)v_0/\|v_0\|$, with the equatorial and fibre orientations fixed in the definition. For the basic left and right quaternion multiplications this degree is $+1$.
entry.strategy: Trivialize over the upper disk and choose the constant nonzero section $v_0=1$. On the lower equator its boundary value is $g(a)1$; the obstruction to extending a nowhere-zero section over the lower disk is its degree. The local Euler obstruction/zero-count characterization identifies this obstruction with the Euler evaluation. Both $a1$ and $1a$ are the identity map of the oriented equator $S^3$, so both degrees are $+1$.

entry.title: Pontryagin calibration of left and right quaternionic clutching
entry.statement: Assume AC. With the preceding clutching, base and fibre orientations, the left multiplication bundle has $e=u$ and $p_1=2u$, while the right multiplication bundle has $e=u$ and $p_1=-2u$.
entry.strategy: Right multiplication by $i$ commutes with left multiplication by every unit quaternion and gives a complex structure whose complex-oriented real basis is $(1,i,j,-k)$, opposite the stipulated quaternionic orientation. Left multiplication by $i$ commutes with right multiplication and gives complex basis $(1,i,j,k)$, agreeing with that orientation. For a complex rank-two bundle $V$, the $\pm i$ eigenspaces of its complexified complex structure give $(V_{\mathbb R})_{\mathbb C}\cong V\oplus\bar V$. Since $H^2(S^4)=0$, the Whitney and conjugation formulas yield $c_2((V_{\mathbb R})_{\mathbb C})=2c_2(V)$ and $p_1(V_{\mathbb R})=-2c_2(V)$. Top Chern equals Euler in the complex orientation, so the left bundle has $c_2=-e=-u$ and the right has $c_2=e=u$. This proves the two signed Pontryagin values.

entry.title: Degree-four characteristic numbers add under clutching product

entry.strategy: The group structure on $\pi_3(SO(4))$ is represented by pointwise multiplication because $SO(4)$ is a topological group. The pinch $S^4\to S^4\vee S^4$ models addition of the two classifying maps. Naturality of universal characteristic classes and the coproduct $[S^4]\mapsto([S^4],[S^4])$ make every degree-four evaluation additive. A null clutching has trivial degree-four classes, so the inverse class has opposite evaluation.

entry.title: Milnor homotopy seven-spheres are topological spheres
entry.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $h+j=\pm1$, $M_{h,j}$ is homeomorphic to $S^7$.
entry.strategy: Remove two disks from the homotopy seven-sphere. The complement is a simply connected seven-dimensional h-cobordism with boundary faces S⁶; it meets the smooth h-cobordism theorem threshold 7≥6. The theorem makes it a smooth cylinder. Reattach the two seven-disks to its ends. One attaching map may be a nonextendable boundary diffeomorphism, but Alexander’s radial extension gives a homeomorphism of the disk; the resulting topological manifold is S⁷. Full AC is inherited from the homology-sphere supplier, and AC implies the h-cobordism supplier’s ACω.

entry.title: Relative Kronecker evaluation is well-defined and natural
entry.statement: For every pair (X,A), abelian coefficient group G and integer k, relative Kronecker evaluation H^k(X,A;G) × H_k(X,A;Z) → G is well-defined, biadditive, coefficient-compatible and natural for maps of pairs. For a commutative unital ring R, R-linear cochains and chains instead give the R-bilinear pairing H^k(X,A;R) × H_k(X,A;R) → R, with the same naturality.
entry.strategy: Represent a relative cochain by a cochain vanishing on simplices in A and a relative cycle z by a chain with ∂z in C(A). Changing z by ∂b+c_A changes evaluation by δα(b)+α(c_A)=0; changing α by δβ changes it by β(∂z)=0. These equations also give bilinearity and naturality. This is the explicit relative contract needed for the pair evaluation maps; the class-level absolute Kronecker supplier alone does not state it. The abelian-group convention uses integral relative chains, as in the exact absolute supplier; the same-ring version uses R-linear cochains on R-chains. No multiplication on an arbitrary abelian group G is assumed.

entry.title: Relative middle cup products are symmetric
entry.statement: For any pair (X,A), the relative degree-four cup product H⁴(X,A;R) × H⁴(X,A;R) → H⁸(X,A;R) is symmetric.
entry.strategy: Use the specified natural chain homotopy H between the Alexander–Whitney diagonal and its factor reversal. Naturality under A→X preserves C(A)⊗C(A), so the cochain primitive in the absolute graded-commutativity proof vanishes on A and descends to relative cochains. Since both degrees are four, the sign is positive. Forgetting either relative factor gives the corresponding relative/absolute symmetry. This supplies the relative symmetry used in the boundary form.

entry.title: Relative cap product evaluation identity
entry.statement: For a relative cohomology class a∈H^p(W,M;R), an absolute class x∈H^{n-p}(W;R), and the relative fundamental class [W,M], one has ⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩=⟨x,a∩[W,M]⟩ in the cohomology-first convention.
entry.strategy: On each singular n-simplex the cap product evaluates a on the front p-face and x on the back (n−p)-face. The resulting cap chain is absolute by the relative cap definition. The cap boundary identity and vanishing of a on M make the chain-level evaluation descend to the relative class. The displayed convention has no extra sign. This is the explicit evaluation bridge used with Poincaré–Lefschetz duality.

entry.title: Collared gluing gives relative excision and evaluation maps
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let W,W′ be compact oriented smooth eight-manifolds glued along an orientation-preserving identification of their common boundary M, and N=W∪_M(−W′). There are natural excision isomorphisms H*(N,V)≅H*(W,M), H*(N,U)≅H*(W′,M), and corresponding relative homology maps. Under them [N] restricts to [W,M] on the first side and to −[W′,M] on the second, compatibly with Kronecker evaluation and relative products.
entry.strategy: Assume ACω for the collar-gluing supplier. Use the collar theorem and smooth gluing/corner-smoothing to form N. In a seam collar M×(−2a,2a), take U=int(W)∪M×(−2a,a) and V=int(W′)∪M×(−a,2a). Each retracts onto its filling and U∩V is the overlap collar. Explicit monotone collar-height homotopies give pair equivalences (U,U∩V)≃(W,M) and (V,U∩V)≃(W′,M). Since the complement of U in N is closed and contained in open V, excision in cohomology gives H*(N,V)≅H*(U,U∩V)≅H*(W,M); likewise for the other side and in homology. Naturality of relative products gives the product comparison. The image of [N] is identified with [W,M] by its local orientation at interior points and the collar boundary-local-homology lemma; on W′ the ambient orientation is reversed, giving −[W′,M]. Pair components lying entirely in one side use absolute relative pairs and the same componentwise argument. Do not extend arbitrary singular cochains by zero across the seam: cover-small excision supplies the chain maps.

entry.title: Compact oriented boundary manifolds have finite-dimensional cohomology
entry.statement: Assume AC. If W is a compact oriented smooth manifold with boundary and F is a field, then every H^k(W;F) and H^k(W,∂W;F) is finite-dimensional.
entry.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from Poincaré–Lefschetz duality and the finite-generation supplier. Double W across a collar to a closed oriented manifold D(W); folding the second copy back gives a retraction D(W)→W, so H_*(W;Z) is a direct summand of the finitely generated homology of D(W). The integral groups are finitely generated. The field UCT identifies cohomology with Hom of finite-dimensional field homology (the Ext term vanishes because vector spaces are free under AC); Poincaré–Lefschetz duality gives the relative groups. This supplies finite-dimensionality without invoking a triangulation theorem.

entry.title: Integral middle cohomology vanishing implies real middle cohomology vanishing
entry.statement: Assume AC. For a closed oriented seven-manifold M, if H³(M;Z)=H⁴(M;Z)=0, then H³(M;R)=H⁴(M;R)=0.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Integral finite generation makes each H_k(M;Z) finitely generated. Apply the universal coefficient short exact sequence with coefficients Z: vanishing H^k implies Hom(H_k,Z)=0, so H_k has zero free part and is finite. With coefficients R, Hom(H_k,R)=0 and Ext(H_{k−1},R)=0, since multiplication by every nonzero integer is onto R. Thus the real cohomology in degrees 3 and 4 vanishes. The finite cyclic resolution verifies the Ext assertion; no integral-to-real substitution is left implicit.

entry.title: Disk-bundle Thom class pairs with the base generator
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let ξ be an oriented rank-four bundle over oriented S⁴ with Euler number ε=±1, W=D(ξ), M=S(ξ), x=π*u, and U the oriented Thom generator. With total orientation base followed by fiber and the induced boundary orientation, ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1.
entry.strategy: Assume AC as required by the Thom, normal-Thom, and duality suppliers. Double W across its collar. The zero section is a closed oriented embedded S⁴ in the double, with normal bundle ξ; the Thom class supported on the W side maps under the excision map to the Poincaré dual of the zero section. Since j(U)=εx, x has relative lift εU, and its restriction to the zero section is u. The closed cap/evaluation identity therefore gives ⟨j_VE_W(U)∪L_W(x),[D(W)]⟩=⟨u,[S⁴]⟩=1. The collar evaluation comparison identifies the left side with ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩. Rank four makes the base/fiber block swap orientation-preserving; this checks the sign. This is the boundary comparison needed before using a Thom normalization in the Pontryagin calculation.

entry.title: Tangent bundle of the Milnor disk bundle has the stable splitting
entry.statement: Assume AC. For W=D(ξ_{h,j}) with projection π:S⁴←W, the stable tangent bundle satisfies TW⊕ε¹≅π*(ξ_{h,j}⊕ε⁵), and p₁(TW)=2(h−j)π*u under the calibrated clutching convention.
entry.strategy: Assume AC for the vector-bundle connection and Pontryagin-class suppliers. The vertical tangent bundle is π*ξ and the quotient of TW by it is π*TS⁴. A smooth connection gives horizontal lifts and splits this exact sequence, so TW≅π*(TS⁴⊕ξ). The explicit map (v,t)↦v+tb identifies TS⁴⊕ε¹ with ε⁵. Hence TW⊕ε¹≅π*(ξ⊕ε⁵). Pontryagin naturality and stability reduce p₁(TW) to π*p₁(ξ)=2(h−j)π*u. This route uses no unproved Whitney cross-term cancellation.

entry.title: Relative middle form and signature for an eight-manifold with boundary
entry.statement: Assume AC as inherited from Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. For a compact oriented smooth eight-manifold $W$ with boundary $M$, let $I=\operatorname{im}(H^4(W,M;\mathbb R)\to H^4(W;\mathbb R))$. A relative lift $\tilde x$ of $x\in I$ defines $Q_W(x,y)=\langle\tilde x\smile y,[W,M]\rangle$. The relative pairing lemma below proves that this is independent of lift, symmetric, and nondegenerate on $I$ after quotienting its radical; define $\sigma(W)$ as the inertia signature of that quotient. This is distinct from the closed-manifold signature of the batch-12 definition.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Define A=H⁴(W,M;R), B=H⁴(W;R), j:A→B and I=im(j); set T(a,x)=⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩. PL duality together with the relative cap/evaluation identity and field UCT gives a perfect pairing A×B. The local finite-dimensionality lemma supplies finite-dimensionality. The formula Q_W(ja,y)=T(a,y) is independent of the lift because a change by ker(j) pairs trivially with I, by exactness/naturality and relative middle-degree symmetry. The same symmetry makes Q symmetric. Perfectness implies the form on I is nondegenerate (so its radical quotient is unchanged); define σ(W) as its inertia signature. This boundary definition is distinct from batch 12’s closed-manifold form.

entry.title: Boundary middle form and Novikov gluing
entry.statement: Assume AC. The relative middle form in the preceding definition is well-defined and symmetric on its nonsingular image quotient. If $W,W\prime$ are compact oriented eight-manifolds with identified oriented boundary $M$ satisfying $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$, then $N=W\cup_M(-W\prime)$ is closed oriented and $\sigma(N)=\sigma(W)-\sigma(W\prime)$.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Work over R and put A=H⁴(W,M;R), B=H⁴(W;R), I=im(j), T(a,x)=⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩. PL duality, the relative cap/evaluation identity, and field UCT give a perfect pairing A×B; finite dimensionality follows from the declared compact-boundary finite-dimensionality lemma. If ja=0, then T(a,jb)=T(b,ja)=0 for all b by relative symmetry, so lift changes pair trivially with I. This proves Q_W is well-defined and symmetric. If x=ja∈I is radical, T(a,jb)=0 for every b, hence T(b,x)=0 for every b; perfectness forces x=0. Thus the image form is already nondegenerate and quotienting its radical leaves it unchanged. Integral H³,H⁴ vanishing implies real vanishing by the declared UCT bridge. For two fillings, the collar/excision/evaluation lemma and MV identify H⁴(N;R) with the two filling groups and identify its closed middle form with Q_W⊕(−Q_W′). Sylvester inertia gives σ(N)=σ(W)−σ(W′). This proves the whole stated scope; the closed signature definition is not being applied directly to W.

entry.title: Disk-bundle middle form and signature
entry.statement: Assume AC. For $h+j=\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, the middle relative form of $W_{h,j}$ is the rank-one form $[\varepsilon]$ generated by the zero section, and $\sigma(W_{h,j})=\varepsilon$. For arbitrary $h,j$, the zero section has self-intersection $h+j$; when this is zero the homological zero-section form is degenerate, while the relative cohomological image I is zero, so its signature is zero.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. The disk bundle retracts onto the oriented zero section S⁴, so its middle absolute cohomology is generated by x=π*u. The zero section has normal bundle ξ_{h,j}; batch 2 self-intersection equals Euler gives square h+j in the boundaryless interior. The relative calculation is explicit: j(U)=εx by the Euler pullback formula, the new Thom/base evaluation lemma gives ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1, and relative/mixed symmetry identifies the image form on x with Q_W(x,x)=ε. For ε=±1 it is the nonsingular rank-one form [ε], with signature ε. When h+j=0, the rank-one homological zero-section form is zero, but j(U)=0 makes the cohomological image I zero-dimensional; its image form is already nonsingular on the zero space and has signature zero. Do not call this image a degenerate rank-one form. Thus the boundary-form comparison, rather than the closed ambient intersection theorem alone, justifies the assertion.

entry.title: Relative square equals mixed evaluation
entry.statement: Let $j:H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)\to H^4(W;\mathbb Z)$ and $a\in H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)$. Then $\langle a\smile a,[W,M]\rangle=\langle a\smile j(a),[W,M]\rangle$, where the left product uses two relative factors and the right uses one relative and one absolute factor.
entry.strategy: Let a be represented by a relative cocycle α on (W,M), so α vanishes on every simplex in M. In the both-relative product take A=B=M; each is open in A∪B=M and C(M)+C(M)=C(M), so the quotient comparison in the relative cup definition is the identity. In the relative/absolute product take A=M,B=∅; its comparison is also the identity. Thus both a∪a and a∪j(a) are represented by exactly α∪α in C⁸(W,M), and their evaluations on [W,M] agree. The relative evaluation pairing is well-defined by the declared local lemma: changing a relative cycle by ∂b+c_M or a cocycle by δβ changes evaluation by zero. This proves the equality directly, without interpreting a boundary square as an absolute degree-eight evaluation.

entry.title: Relative Pontryagin square of a Milnor disk bundle
entry.statement: Assume AC. If $h+j=\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ and $k=h-j$, then the unique relative lift $\bar p_1\in H^4(W_{h,j},M_{h,j};\mathbb Z)$ of $p_1(TW_{h,j})$ exists and $q(W_{h,j}):=\langle\bar p_1\smile\bar p_1,[W_{h,j},M_{h,j}]\rangle=4\varepsilon k^2$.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Put ε=h+j=±1, k=h−j, x=π*u, and let U be the oriented Thom generator. The tangent splitting lemma gives p₁(TW)=2kx. The Thom theorem identifies H⁴(W,M)=ZU and H⁴(W)=Zx; Euler pullback gives j(U)=εx, so the unique relative lift is bar p₁=2kεU. The disk-bundle Thom/base evaluation lemma proves ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1 with the base-followed-by-fiber orientation. The relative-square/mixed-evaluation lemma then gives q(W)=⟨bar p₁²,[W,M]⟩=⟨(2kεU)∪(2kx),[W,M]⟩=4εk². The integrality and ε=±1 hypothesis are essential.

entry.title: Milnor lambda candidate from a supplied filling
entry.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth seven-manifold with $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$, and let $W$ be a supplied compact oriented smooth eight-manifold with $\partial W=M$. The pair sequence makes $j:H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)\to H^4(W;\mathbb Z)$ an isomorphism. Define $\bar p_1(W)=j^{-1}p_1(TW)$, $q(W)=\langle\bar p_1(W)\smile\bar p_1(W),[W,M]\rangle$, and the filling-level candidate $\lambda_W(M)=2q(W)-\sigma(W)\pmod7$. This definition asserts no general existence of $W$ and no independence of $W$; both are separate questions.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Let M be closed oriented seven-dimensional with integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0, and let a compact oriented filling W be supplied. The pair-sequence segment H³(M)→H⁴(W,M)→H⁴(W)→H⁴(M) proves that j is an integral isomorphism: H³=0 gives uniqueness, H⁴=0 gives existence. Define bar p₁=j⁻¹p₁(TW), q(W)=⟨bar p₁∪bar p₁,[W,M]⟩, and λ_W=2q(W)−σ(W) mod 7 using the boundary-form definition. The relative-square/mixed-evaluation lemma validates the relative product evaluation. This is conditional on a supplied bound and asserts neither a universal bounding theorem nor filling independence.

entry.title: Relative Pontryagin squares glue to the closed Pontryagin number
entry.statement: Assume AC. Under the hypotheses of the lambda-candidate definition for two fillings W,W′ of the same oriented M, let N=W∪_M(−W′). Then ⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩=q(W)−q(W′). Orientation reversal changes evaluation signs, not the Pontryagin class itself.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. Let W,W′ fill the same M and N=W∪_M(−W′). The pair sequence segment H³(M)→H⁴(W,M)→H⁴(W)→H⁴(M), with both boundary groups zero, makes each relative-to-absolute map an integral isomorphism. MV on the explicit collar cover U,V gives H⁴(N)≅H⁴(W)⊕H⁴(W′). For x∈H⁴(W), excision extends its unique relative lift from (W,M) to (N,V), then forgets relative conditions to a class L_W(x) with restrictions (x,0); similarly L_W′(x′) has restrictions (0,x′). MV uniqueness shows p₁(TN)=L_W(p₁(TW))+L_W′(p₁(TW′)): the tangent charts glue across the seam with the normal coordinate reversed, giving a real bundle isomorphism, while p₁ is orientation-independent. Cross products vanish because the extended factors lie in H⁸(N,U∪V)=H⁸(N,N)=0 via the excisive relative product; do not claim arbitrary singular cochains extended by zero are cochains. Same-side product naturality plus the relative excision/evaluation lemma gives the W evaluation q(W), and −q(W′) on the oppositely oriented second half. Expanding the square therefore yields ⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩=q(W)−q(W′). This is a complete local route; the actual item body still needs authoring.

entry.title: Milnor lambda is an oriented boundary invariant modulo seven
entry.statement: Assume AC. For a closed oriented smooth seven-manifold $M$ with $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$ and at least one supplied compact oriented smooth eight-dimensional filling, $\lambda(M):=2q(W)-\sigma(W)\in\mathbb Z/7$ is independent of the filling and invariant under orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphism. Reversing the orientation of $M$ negates $\lambda(M)$.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. For two supplied fillings glue N=W∪_M(−W′). The relative Pontryagin-square comparison gives q(W)−q(W′)=⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩, and the boundary-form gluing lemma gives σ(W)−σ(W′)=σ(N). Batch 12’s closed eight-dimensional formula, applied only to closed N, says 45σ(N)=7⟨p₂(TN),[N]⟩−⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩. Modulo 7, 3σ+p₁²=0, so p₁²=4σ and 2p₁²−σ=0. Substitution proves λ_W=λ_W′. An orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphism transports a filling with collars and preserves this comparison. Reversing orientation negates fundamental-class evaluations and signature while fixing p₁, hence negates λ. No filling existence for every M is asserted.

entry.title: Milnor’s exotic seven-sphere
entry.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. $M_{2,-1}$ is homeomorphic to $S^7$ but is not diffeomorphic to it. More generally, for $h+j=1$, the constructed sphere has $\lambda(M_{h,j})=(h-j)^2-1\pmod7$; a nonzero value obstructs a diffeomorphism to the standard sphere even without a prescribed orientation.
entry.strategy: Assume AC. For ε=h+j=1 and k=h−j, the disk-bundle relative Pontryagin calculation gives q=4k² and its boundary form gives σ=1, so λ=8k²−1≡k²−1 mod 7. At (h,j)=(2,−1), k=3 and λ=8≡1; the standard sphere bounds D⁸ with q=σ=0. The lambda theorem makes this an obstruction to an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. If an orientation-reversing diffeomorphism existed, the standard sphere’s zero invariant would still be zero under negation, contradicting λ=1. Separately, the homology/Gysin and Whitehead steps give a homotopy sphere; its two-disk complement is a seven-dimensional h-cobordism between S⁶ ends, within dimension≥6, so the batch-15 h-cobordism theorem gives a cylinder and the radial Alexander extension supplies a homeomorphism after reattaching disks. The topological recognition route is separate from the characteristic invariant.

entry.title: The quaternionic Hopf sphere bundle
entry.statement: Assume AC. $M_{1,0}\cong S^7$ by the quaternionic Hopf fibration, with $e(\xi_{1,0})=u$, $p_1(\xi_{1,0})=2u$, and $\lambda(M_{1,0})=0$.

The class formula gives $e=u,p_1=2u$, and the disk-bundle computation gives $\lambda=1^2-1=0$.

entry.title: Topological type does not determine smooth type
entry.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The standard $S^7$ and $M_{2,-1}$ are homeomorphic closed seven-manifolds but are not diffeomorphic. Thus homeomorphism type does not determine smooth structure in dimension seven.
entry.strategy: The topological identification and nonzero lambda obstruction are established by the main Milnor theorem; the two structures form the claimed counterexample.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405
